claims.text: Minor-element substitution can change the alloy's average atomic mass.
Minor-element substitution can change local lattice distortion in the alloy.
Changes in average atomic mass and local lattice distortion alter the phonon density of states.
Changes in the phonon density of states alter electron–phonon coupling strength.
Electron–phonon coupling strength governs the superconducting transition temperature in the proposed high-entropy alloy.
The starting material is a single-phase solid-solution alloy containing at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
The starting alloy is superconducting and has an established transition temperature.
The intervention replaces approximately 5–10 atomic percent of one constituent with a lighter or heavier element.
The substitution-induced mass contrast and local lattice distortion modify the phonon density of states.
Changing average atomic mass and bonding dynamics shifts lattice phonon modes.
The shifted phonon modes modify the electron–phonon coupling responsible for superconductivity.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling raises the superconducting transition temperature, whereas weakened coupling lowers it.
The substituted alloy will exhibit a measurable shift in superconducting transition temperature relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains a phase-homogeneous solid solution without secondary phases or long-range ordering.
The magnitude and sign of the transition-temperature shift depend on the substituted element and inter-element interactions.
